editorial:
Imagine having the worst day of your life, getting fired, and then deciding to hide in a piece of furniture just to escape the world. That is exactly what happens to Sergio, a carpenter who ends up trapped in a closet that gets sold and delivered to a random family's home. You get to watch this weird, tense situation unfold as he lives in the walls, spying on the people who now own his hiding spot. It starts off feeling like a strange prank, but it quickly turns into a creepy game of cat and mouse where you never know if he will be caught in the next five minutes.

The acting is great because most of the tension comes from Sergio's face and his quiet reactions. The pacing is steady, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you want non-stop action. However, the payoff is worth it. If you are into stories about secrets and people hiding in plain sight, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection if you want the best picture quality possible.
endingExplained: In the end, Sergio's secret life crashes down when the family finally discovers him. The tension peaks as he is forced to face the people he has been spying on for so long. Instead of a happy ending, you see the messy results of his obsession. He realizes that hiding from his problems didn't fix his life, and the movie wraps up by showing that some secrets are too big to stay hidden forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and stories about creepy intruders.
